clue.text: Nunnery has a lion under control? Correct!

parts.note: a convent is a community house of nuns

indicators.note: taken in hand, these letters are brought into a new order

explanation.surface: A convent keeping a tamed lion asks whether that is proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under control' rearranges A LION into IONAL, which follows CONVENT; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional behaviour is proper and orthodox, which is what a correct manner means.

clue.text: Cuts possibly made about one in charge are severe

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are put around the single letter
the letters of cuts might be rearranged

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Budget cuts arranged by a manager are harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns CUTS into CUST, which 'made about' wraps around A; IC follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting, harsh remarks are scathing, which is what severe criticism means.

clue.text: Crass f-football follower stands on his head

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: the stammered letter F
a fan supports a football team

explanation.surface: A stuttering, tasteless football supporter does a headstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands on his head' turns F + FAN upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for tacky or lacking style, much like vulgar.

clue.text: Where the cross peer got a denial in France

indicators.note: a cross peer is out of sorts, so his letters are jumbled

parts.note: nay is a refusal

explanation.surface: An angry nobleman was refused somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' rearranges PEER to EPER; 'in France' tells the solver the place is French. ÉPERNAY is a Champagne town.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the Champagne region, a place, as asked for by the question word.

clue.text: Checking to see if the fare is all right

definitions.text: Checking to see if the fare is all right

parts.words: Checking to see if the fare is all right
parts.note: fare reads like a ticket price but means food, checked by sampling it

explanation.surface: A conductor seems to be inspecting tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampling food to judge its flavour is how a cook checks a dish.

clue.text: Dummies found in ruined sofa

indicators.note: a wrecked sofa has its letters broken up and reset

explanation.surface: Mannequins discovered in a wrecked settee.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummies are clumsy dolts, as are louts of low intelligence.

clue.text: With hidden energy, Ali on a restored harp

indicators.note: the energy letter is tucked inside the other letters
the letters of Ali on a are put back in a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Ali puts some vigour into repairing a harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges ALI ON A and 'With hidden' places E inside. The Aeolian harp is played by wind.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aeolian harp is one sounded by wind, named after Aeolus, god of the winds, so the adjective stands for the instrument.

clue.text: Monroe supporters say NATO's oil is its undoing

indicators.note: the words are undone and their letters reassembled

parts.note: NATO with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Some claim that NATO's petrol policy is ruining it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Monroe Doctrine kept the US out of European affairs; 'Monroe' tempts towards Marilyn.
explanation.definitionFit: Backers of the US policy of staying out of foreign entanglements, as President Monroe's doctrine urged.

clue.text: Blade entering ship is fun for kids

parts.note: a skate is a boot with a blade
boarding means going aboard a vessel

explanation.surface: A child's blade getting onto a ship is great sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a wheeled plank is a popular pastime for youngsters.

clue.text: Drag one's feet prior to dealing

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles before handing out cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle is to walk without lifting the feet, and cards are mixed by a shuffle before a deal.

clue.text: Endless row coming up over people in county

indicators.note: the first piece sits ahead of the second
in a down-style reading the letters rise, so the shortened word is read backwards
the final letter of the row word is cut off, leaving it without an end

parts.note: a row is a noisy fuss or commotion
folk means people in general

explanation.surface: A dispute keeps surfacing among the residents of an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims FUSS to FUS and 'coming up' turns it to SUF, put before FOLK. SUFFOLK is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is an English shire on the North Sea coast, an example of a county.

clue.text: Departed or not yet arrived?

explanation.surface: A riddle over whether someone has gone or has not come yet.
explanation.definitionFit: The departed are the deceased, called 'the late'; a train not yet in is overdue or tardy.

clue.text: From Cremona I returned exalted

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words Cremona I returned

explanation.surface: A traveller says they came back from the Italian city of violins.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Cremona I returned'; 'returned' looks like a reversal signal but is only part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Being broadcast lifts a voice up into the airwaves, loosely an elevated or lofty state.

clue.text: Can it turn the tide for the overweight?

definitions.text: Can it turn the tide for the overweight?

indicators.note: turning these letters around jumbles them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Asks whether something might reverse the trend for heavy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges TIDE; the whole clue also describes what a slimming regime aims to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimming regime of controlled eating is the usual remedy for excess weight.

clue.text: Unfairly 'e hurt Arthur's Dad

indicators.note: treated unjustly, the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A cockney complains a man hurt King Arthur's father.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend, Uther Pendragon is King Arthur's father.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther Pendragon fathered the legendary king of Camelot.

clue.text: Pound up a street with dynamite

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters rise, reading backwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone batters a road with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LB into BL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dynamite something is to blow it up with explosives.

clue.text: Silently, cattily, oddly

indicators.note: arranged in a strange way, the letters of cattily are mixed up

explanation.surface: Three adverbs describing someone sniping quietly and strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without words means unspoken, implied rather than voiced aloud.

clue.text: Crosby upset about ageing but valuable writer

indicators.note: the reversed name goes around the word for ageing
knocked over, the singer's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the American crooner
ageing means getting old

explanation.surface: A crooner, now old, is upset yet still a precious author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BING into GNIB, and 'about' wraps it around OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen point made of precious metal is a costly writing implement.

clue.text: Nothing at breakfast, lunch dinner but porridge

parts.note: zero, the round letter O
each is a kind of repast

explanation.surface: Someone eats nothing all day except a bowl of porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is cooked from ground oats, so the ground grain names the dish.

clue.text: Language used to label a record

parts.note: a tag is a label
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A tongue employed for tagging an entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The main tongue of the Philippines, a spoken language.

clue.text: Prepared for an awkward guy getting outside help

indicators.note: the fellow goes around the word for help

parts.note: a lout is a clumsy, boorish fellow
aid means help

explanation.surface: Something is set up for a clumsy man who needs assistance outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Set out ready, arranged in advance, as a prepared meal or plan.

clue.text: Exclamation of those central to a girl

indicators.note: only the inner letters of the word those are used

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone cries out about a girl among a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of praise or adoration to God, an interjection used in worship.

clue.text: John Peel crazy for seedy fruit?

parts.note: the huntsman of the folk song is famed for his horn, which stands for him here
nut means a crazy person, or nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: The famous huntsman goes mad over a fruit full of seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: D'ye ken John Peel is an English hunting song whose hero rouses all with his horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The water chestnut, a nut-like seed, is so called; the question mark flags a loose sense of fruit.

clue.text: The heart of the matter

parts.note: the phrase means the central point, but in physics an atom's core is literally the centre of matter

explanation.surface: The essential point of an issue.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of an atom or cell, the central part around which everything gathers.

clue.text: One silver ring for an ancient mind-poisoner

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A single silver ring passes to an old schemer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' is the old word for an ensign: Othello's ensign poisons his mind with jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's ensign villain poisons Othello's thoughts; ensign was called 'ancient' in Elizabethan English.

clue.text: It's up to a painter to provide the jewellery

indicators.note: in this reading the word is raised and so reads backwards

parts.note: the word it, with the possessive ending giving no letter
RA, a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: It falls to an artist to supply the jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT to TI; RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled headband or coronet is an item of ornamental adornment.

clue.text: Top-class deputy head gave unbeatable service

parts.note: ace means excellent

indicators.note: only the leading letter of deputy is taken

explanation.surface: An excellent deputy head served an unreturnable ball at tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch, so to have served one is past tense.

clue.text: The sound of jive can reduce one to hobbling

indicators.note: the spoken word is matched by another spelling

parts.note: jive is a lively dance

explanation.surface: Dancing the jive can leave someone limping.
explanation.walkthrough: GYVE is an old word for a fetter or leg iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A shackle on the leg leaves a prisoner able only to limp.

clue.text: Row back in a knot

indicators.note: the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rank is a row or line

explanation.surface: A row snarled up into a tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a gnarl in wood, a bump or knob in a tree's grain.

clue.text: Hotspur's leaders score first hunting cry

indicators.note: the score word comes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a tally is a running score

indicators.note: the opening letters of Hotspur are taken

explanation.surface: Hotspur's captains rack up points before the hunt sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first two letters of Hotspur, HO, and 'first' puts TALLY before them.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxhunters shout this call when the quarry is sighted.

clue.text: Ann could be enthusiastic with the material

indicators.note: the letters of Ann could become a different arrangement

parts.note: keen means eager or enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Ann might be excited about the fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ANN to NAN, followed by KEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff-coloured cotton cloth originally from Nanjing, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Put one's name to a HP contract?

definitions.text: Put one's name to a HP contract?

parts.words: Put one's name to a HP contract?
parts.note: signing a hire-purchase deal means accepting its instalment schedule, a pun on the paying periods

explanation.surface: Someone signs a hire-purchase agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is hire purchase, the British system of buying goods in instalments over set periods.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept the conditions offered is to settle a deal, as one does on signing.
